item: The storage-events journal records the first event of a pool timeout and of a gate hold (first_seen_at) at the event, beside the kept sample, so the first bad hour no longer moves with the sample
summary: Two bundles of one process put the first bad hour of the pool at 16:00 in one and 15:00 in the other (10 of 1,575 pool timeouts kept, then 10 of 1,362): the reader took the oldest KEPT event as the onset, and the keep rule moves it. storage_events.ONSET_KINDS (gate_hold, pool_timeout) now carry first_seen_at, the at of the kind's first event ever, set under the journal lock when the event is recorded (the stamp is taken under the same lock, so the onset is never later than an event it counts), written with the counters and read back across restarts; the file's value wins over this process's. total is the count since it (both start at the kind's first event), so no second count is stored. An onset that is not known is null with first_seen_unknown: 'not-recorded' for a file that counted events before the field existed, 'history-unread' while the earlier file cannot be read (this process's first event is not the first ever). The zip budget cuts events and splits, never the onset. Bytes: the member is cut to its 125,000 slot; the two keys add 88 and the method and caveat are 39 shorter with the new sentence in them, so the fixed part grows 5,129 to 5,178; at the widest names the same 5 of 20 splits are kept with 17 bytes free (was 66), ordinary names 43,468 free; with an unknown onset the widest names keep 4 splits, no event is dropped. Mutants killed: onset read off the sample (member, file write, file read), reset on every record, not written, new process overriding, min instead of the file's, legacy taking the new first, junk accepted, no reason, every kind carrying it, cut with the events, set by a refused record, stamped before the lock, shown while the history is unread.
